text: The two lads who slept in the loft
why: Paragraph 19: one lad sat up in the stable and the others slept in the loft, so two lads slept there.

text: The four horses at King's Pyland
why: Paragraph 19: 'containing only four horses in all.'

text: The small cluster of villas to the north
why: Paragraph 19: 'about half a mile to the north there is a small cluster of villas.'
Paragraph 19: the villas 'have been built by a Tavistock contractor.'
Paragraph 19: 'Tavistock itself lies two miles to the west.'
Paragraph 19: across the moor, about two miles off, is 'the larger training establishment of Mapleton.'

Paragraph 19: the moor is 'inhabited only by a few roaming gypsies.'

text: Years before, while Straker served Colonel Ross as jockey and then as trainer
why: Paragraph 19: Straker rode for Colonel Ross 'as jockey' for five years and 'as trainer' for seven, so the earlier jockey period precedes the trainer period.

text: What has become of the favourite? — at Mapleton
why: Asks a plain question the story has given reason to ask (the favourite is missing and Mapleton is a rival stable nearby). 'At Mapleton' is one possibility a reader could reasonably consider, not a stated fact.

text: What has become of the favourite? — with the gypsies
why: Asks the same plain question; the story has mentioned gypsies as the only people roaming the moor and Holmes has remarked the horse could not stay hidden in a sparsely inhabited area, so this is a possibility a reader has reason to consider.
